messages:
amanda: Heads-up — got a support ticket where a customer was charged ~3x tokens vs what the UI showed. They were using streaming + a toolcall that retries on 5xx. Repro steps attached.
raj: ugh. Do we have a tracing id or request id for that session?
amanda: yes, request_id=rid_8a3f. I pasted the logs: 
```
[2026-03-12T13:02:11Z] RID=rid_8a3f stream:init prefix_len=1024 model=redwood-1 size_out=512
[2026-03-12T13:02:13Z] RID=rid_8a3f toolcall:invoke attempt=1 code=502
[2026-03-12T13:02:13Z] RID=rid_8a3f toolcall:retry attempt=2
[2026-03-12T13:02:13Z] RID=rid_8a3f kv:evict evicted_prefix_bytes=640
[2026-03-12T13:02:14Z] RID=rid_8a3f stream:resume prefix_len=384 billed_tokens=1536
```

amanda: Billing shows billed_tokens=1536 (prefix accounting + resumed stream). UI final token count displayed 512. Support says customer got charged for the evicted prefix again after retry.

tim: Quick hypothesis: when the toolcall fails and we retry, the prefix that was in KV got evicted (due to memory pressure) and when we resume we reconstruct the prompt by prepending the prefix bytes back — but the accounting path double-counts because streaming accounting counts both the original prefix and the reconstructed prefix during resume.

olga: That matches our old race where stream accounting increments on chunk send and toolcall retry also reconciles prefix accounting. We thought the eviction case was rare. Looks like retries + small mem cap triggers it.

raj: Can we repro in a unit/integration test? Simulate KV eviction between attempts and assert billed tokens equals unique tokens served (dedupe by prefix checksum)?

amanda: I wrote a quick curl flow to reproduce locally: start streaming with small kv_capacity, trigger toolcall 502 then allow eviction. I can push repro script to a branch if ppl want.

tim: Please do. In parallel, we should consider a short-term metric guard: emit a gauge 'stream/resumed_duplicate_token_count' whenever resumed_prefix_bytes > 0 && evicted_prefix_bytes > 0. Add a dashboard panel so support can triage.

olga: Agreed. Also need to decide accounting semantics: on resume after eviction+rebuild, we should credit the original prefix billing and mark resumed tokens as delta-only. Option: keep a request-local prefix checksum set — if a prefix with same checksum already billed, skip re-billing.

raj: checksum set sounds safe and small. But we must ensure it survives restarts for long-lived streams? We only need it across retries inside the same request lifetime. So in-memory per-request is fine.

amanda: Edgecases: what if a user legitimately modifies the prefix (toolcall changed system prompt)? Then checksum differs and we should bill the new prefix. We need to capture a stable canonicalization for prefix before counting (whitespace normalization, tokens->counts).

tim: Implementation plan: 1) add request-scoped set of billed_prefix_checksums 2) before billing a prefix chunk, compute checksum and dedupe 3) emit metric when dedupe occurs 4) add unit tests for eviction+retry+modified-prefix

olga: UX/rollout: ship behind a feature flag default on for hosted, opt-in for dedicated for a week, then full rollout. We should also add a migration doc for private deployments (small patch no DB changes).

raj: Also update token-level debug trace in the console so support can show 'prefix_checksum' in the per-call trace. That will reduce back-and-forth.

amanda: I'll open a PR for the checksum + metric. Can someone own the dashboard panel?

tim: I can add a Graf panel and an Alerts rule (warning at >5 duplicated tokens/min for a tenant).

olga: I'll add unit/integration tests and a short runbook snippet for support.

infrabot: Deploy plan created: pr/feature/kvc-dedupe -> canary (5% traffic) -> 25% -> 100%. Smoke tests include stream-retry-eviction scenario.

amanda: thanks. If anyone sees other weird billing diffs, paste request ids here. I'll track in the support ticket. :thumbsup:
